request.system:
You compare two draft pieces of marketing copy for Wedding Industry Ads (WIA), a wedding-industry advertising agency. You are given the request, the version WIA's co-founder Whitney actually approved or wrote (the reference), and two candidate drafts. Decide which candidate would need fewer and smaller edits to become something Whitney would approve. Judge substance first (what is claimed, for whom, how WIA is positioned, accuracy, whether her own wording was kept where she supplied it), then voice. Do not reward length, and do not require the candidate to copy the reference wording.

Return only JSON: {"winner": "A" or "B" or "tie", "edits_needed_A": "few", "edits_needed_B": "many", "reason": "one or two sentences"} where edits_needed values are none, few, some or many.

Below is the transcript of a reel I'm going to post tomorrow. I need a caption to go along with it. 

It needs to appeal to venues/wedding pros who want consistent lead generation and profitable ads (regardless of if they would be a better fit for Elevate or the Accelerators)

From recent market research, most respondents said that their biggest problem before working with us wasn't getting in front of enough clients consistently. What's most important to them about making an investment like this was split evenly between:

-having a clear strategy and confidence investment will generate strong return
-seeing efficient progress and knowing I'm making a smart move for my business

Most said that what would hold them back is:
"I'd want to be confident the strategy will actually bring in quality inquiries, not just more leads"

CTA can be to visit our link in bio to learn about the ways they can work with us

Daniela: And to be fair, it's not that organic marketing doesn't have a place in 2026 or moving forward. It's that ads can help create more stability around lead generation specifically. And then that way when people do go over to your website or they do go over to your Instagram profile or whatever your social accounts are that you use, there's something relevant there for them to consume. But the point of entry is where you can control them.



Whitney: Yeah. And so we've got the points of entry on Google with Google search. We can run paid campaigns there, right? To make sure that you are showing up in the search results for the exact keywords that you want to be showing up for for couples who are searching with high intent. They want to find a venue or a vendor just like you. 



Daniela: People are booking wedding vendors from Google searches, but oftentimes when people are searching, they'll hit your website and then they might click away. You can make sure that the people who have landed on your website, even if they're not following you, that they're able to consume the content that you're putting so much work into creating, right? Reference (what Whitney approved):
One thing we hear often from wedding pros before they work with us is:

“I don’t want my ads to feel generic.”
“I want to know the leads coming in are actually aligned.”
“I just want to feel confident I’m making a smart investment.”

And honestly, that hesitation makes complete sense.

The wedding industry is full of agencies promising more leads without understanding positioning, buyer psychology, or what actually turns quality inquiries into booked clients.

Most business owners aren’t looking for flashy marketing.

They’re looking for a strategy that feels intentional, brand-aligned, and capable of generating real ROI long-term.

Candidate A:
Your next booking shouldn’t depend on whether a couple happens to find you.

You can have a beautiful brand, an excellent client experience, and an Instagram full of work you’re proud of—and still wonder where next month’s inquiries will come from.

That doesn’t mean your business needs more content. It may need a more intentional way to bring the right couples into it.

Organic marketing helps couples get to know you. Paid ads can help more of the right people discover you—and give them reasons to come back.

Google Search can put you in front of couples actively looking for a venue or service like yours. Meta can help you stay visible while they compare options and decide who to trust.

But visibility alone isn’t the goal.

**The goal is quality inquiries that turn into profitable bookings.**

That takes more than an ad campaign. Your messaging, landing page, and follow-up all need to help couples feel confident taking the next step.

That’s the problem we solve at Wedding Industry Ads: the gap between having a business couples would love and having a reliable system to help them find—and choose—it.

We’ve helped wedding businesses double their business, grow their teams, and feel more confident in the marketing supporting their growth.

Not by treating every wedding business the same. By understanding their goals, building a strategy around them, and looking beyond clicks to the sales conversations and bookings that matter.

Whether you want a team to manage your ads or guidance to learn how to manage them yourself, you deserve to understand the strategy—and feel supported by the people helping you put it into practice.

You don’t need to arrive knowing which platform or level of support is right for you.

**Visit the link in our bio to explore the ways to work with us and find the right fit for your business.**
